method: Each claim checked against the retrieved text of the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Febrile child' (PIC endorsed), including key points, background, history, examination and the unwell-child feature table, management, the infants-28-days-or-less section, consultation, transfer, discharge, additional notes on temperature measurement, lumbar puncture, urine collection and blood culture, the blood culture volume table, and the reference list. Every source_text fragment was machine-checked verbatim against the retrieved source with scripts/verify.py. The management algorithms for infants 29 days to 3 months and children over 3 months are flowchart IMAGES and were not retrieved: they are recorded as input_unavailable and are not reconstructed, and the guideline states that it cannot be used to triage those age groups. Empiric antibiotic choice and dose are deferred by the source to local antimicrobial guidelines and are not stated or reconstructed. The page states 'Last update September 2022' while both flowcharts are filenamed Feb2025; this discrepancy is recorded as time_sensitive rather than resolved.

claims.claim: Key point 1 is that febrile neonates 28 days or less of corrected age require investigations being FBE, CRP, blood, urine and CSF cultures plus or minus CXR, and empiric IV antibiotic therapy
claims.source_text: 1. Febrile neonates ≤28 days of corrected age require investigations (FBE, CRP, blood, urine and CSF cultures ± CXR) and empiric IV antibiotic therapy

claims.claim: Key point 2 is that in febrile infants over 28 days of corrected age and under 3 months, clinicians should have a low threshold for investigation and treatment based on clinical appearance and presence or absence of a clinically obvious focus
claims.source_text: 2. In Febrile infants >28 days of corrected age and <3 months, have a low threshold for investigation and treatment based on clinical appearance and presence (or absence) of a clinically obvious focus

claims.claim: Key point 3 is that in infants under 3 months of age, hypothermia or temperature instability can be signs of serious bacterial infection or other serious illness
claims.source_text: 3. In infants <3 months of age, hypothermia or temperature instability can be signs of serious bacterial infection (or other serious illness)

claims.claim: The severity of illness cannot be predicted by the degree of fever, its rapidity of onset, its response to antipyretics or the presence of febrile seizures, and the appearance of the child is the most useful indicator
claims.source_text: 4. The severity of illness cannot be predicted by the degree of fever, its rapidity of onset, its response to antipyretics or the presence of febrile seizures; the appearance of the child is the most useful indicator

claims.claim: Fever is defined as body temperature greater than 38.0 degrees Celsius
claims.source_text: Definition of fever: body temperature >38.0º Celsius

claims.claim: Where possible clinicians should use the same body site and the same type of thermometer when measuring temperatures
claims.source_text: Where possible, use the same body site and the same type of thermometer when measuring temperatures

claims.claim: The most common causes of fever in children are viral infections however serious bacterial infections need to be considered, and the most common serious bacterial infections found in children without a focus are urinary tract infections
claims.source_text: The most common causes of fever in children are viral infections, however serious bacterial infections (SBIs) need to be considered … The most common SBIs found in children without a focus are urinary tract infections

claims.claim: Since the introduction of the pneumococcal vaccine the rate of occult bacteraemia has fallen to less than 1 per cent in healthy immunised children
claims.source_text: Since the introduction of the pneumococcal vaccine, the rate of occult bacteraemia has fallen to <1% in healthy, immunised children

claims.claim: Children with fever for 5 days or more should be assessed for Kawasaki disease or PIMS-TS if there is a history of COVID-19 infection
claims.source_text: Children with fever for ≥5 days should be assessed for Kawasaki disease or PIMS-TS if there is a history of COVID-19 infection

claims.claim: Other uncommon causes of prolonged fever in children include inflammatory, immune-mediated and neoplastic conditions and specialist input may be required
claims.source_text: Other uncommon causes of prolonged fever in children include inflammatory, immune-mediated and neoplastic conditions; specialist input may be required

claims.claim: History should cover localising symptoms such as cough, headache, photophobia, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal pain, musculoskeletal pain and rash
claims.source_text: Localising symptoms eg cough, headache, photophobia, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal pain, musculoskeletal pain, rash

claims.claim: Prior treatment with antibiotics may mask signs of a bacterial infection
claims.source_text: Medication: prior treatment with antibiotics may mask signs of a bacterial infection

claims.claim: High risk factors include prematurity, immunosuppression or oncological conditions, central line in situ, chronic lung disease, congenital heart disease, previous invasive bacterial infections, children of Aboriginal, Torres Strait Islander, Pacific Islander or Maori origin, and multiple health service presentations

claims.claim: Teething does not cause fever
claims.source_text: Teething does not cause fever

claims.source_text: Post vaccination fever is common, with a typical onset within 24 hours of immunisation and duration up to 2-3 days; however, in an unwell child, fever should not be attributed to vaccination alone

claims.claim: Clinicians should not accept apparent otitis media or upper respiratory symptoms as the source of infection in young infants or unwell children, and these children still require assessment for possible serious bacterial infection
claims.source_text: Do not accept apparent otitis media or upper respiratory symptoms as the source of infection in young infants or unwell children. These children still require assessment for possible SBI

claims.claim: If the child is stable it is preferable to complete investigations looking for an infective focus before commencing antibiotics, and in children from high risk groups clinicians should have a lower threshold for investigations
claims.source_text: If the child is stable, it is preferable to complete investigations looking for an infective focus before commencing antibiotics … In children from high risk groups, have a lower threshold for investigations

claims.claim: For infants 28 days or less of corrected age clinicians should assess promptly for signs of sepsis and discuss with a senior doctor, perform FBE, CRP, blood culture, urine by suprapubic aspirate, LP plus or minus CXR, and give prompt treatment with empiric antibiotics
claims.source_text: Assess promptly for signs of sepsis and discuss with a senior doctor. … FBE, CRP, blood culture, urine (by SPA; see section on Urine collection below for other methods), LP ± CXR

claims.claim: If the infant appears unwell or there is likely to be a delay in completing all of the required investigations, clinicians should proceed with administration of antibiotics
claims.source_text: If the infant appears unwell, or there is likely to be a delay in completing all of the required investigations, proceed with administration of antibiotics

claims.claim: Consultation with the local paediatric team should be considered for an unwell child, septic shock, infants under 28 days corrected age with fever who should be admitted for empiric antibiotics, barriers to follow-up within 24 hours due to social or external factors where admission should be considered, a high-risk child, advice needed regarding empiric treatment, and prolonged fever of unclear cause
claims.source_text: Infants <28 days corrected age with fever (should be admitted for empiric antibiotics) … Barriers to follow-up within 24 hours due to social or external factors (consider admission)

claims.claim: Transfer to a tertiary centre should be considered for a child requiring care above the level of comfort of the local hospital
claims.source_text: Child requiring care above the level of comfort of the local hospital

claims.claim: Discharge may be considered for infants 29 days to 3 months of corrected age when they are well, investigations are normal, the case has been discussed with a senior doctor and follow-up within 12 to 24 hours has been arranged, and for children over 3 months corrected age when they are well and follow up has been arranged
claims.source_text: Infants 29 days to 3 months of corrected age: well, investigations normal, discussed with senior doctor, follow-up within 12-24 hours has been arranged … Children >3 months corrected age: well, follow up has been arranged

claims.claim: Parents should always be advised to return for review if the child is deteriorating
claims.source_text: Always advise parents to return for review if the child is deteriorating

claims.claim: Axillary temperature is recommended for infants under 3 months of age and for a more accurate reading the thermometer should be placed over the axillary artery for 3 minutes
claims.source_text: Axillary temperature: recommended for infants <3 months of age … For a more accurate reading, the thermometer should be placed over the axillary artery for 3 minutes.

claims.claim: Tympanic temperature is recommended for children over 3 months of age and for an accurate measurement the pinna must be retracted to straighten the external auditory meatus and the instrument should be directed at the tympanic membrane
claims.source_text: Tympanic temperature: recommended for children >3 months of age. For an accurate measurement, the pinna must be retracted to straighten the external auditory meatus and the instrument should be directed at the tympanic membrane.

claims.claim: Skin temperature measurement using forehead or infrared thermometers is unreliable

claims.claim: For rectal temperature in neonates clinicians should screen first with axillary temperature then consider performing a rectal temperature if a fever is still suspected

claims.claim: When indicated, lumbar puncture should be performed without delay and ideally before the administration of antibiotics

claims.source_text: Contraindications to LP include impaired conscious state, focal neurological signs, impaired coagulation or haemodynamic instability

claims.claim: Where there are contraindications to lumbar puncture, treatment for meningitis or encephalitis should be commenced and an LP performed when the child is stable and there are no contraindications

claims.claim: Bag urine specimens should never be sent for culture due to high false positive rates, with a contamination rate of 50 per cent
claims.source_text: Bag urine specimens should never be sent for culture due to high false positive rates - contamination rate 50%

claims.claim: Suprapubic aspirate is the gold standard for urine collection with a contamination rate of 1 per cent, and in/out catheter is useful if there is little urine in the bladder such as after failed clean catch or SPA with a contamination rate of 10 per cent

claims.claim: Midstream urine is the preferred method for toilet-trained children who can void on request with a contamination rate of 25 per cent, and clean catch is appropriate for pre-continent children who cannot void on request but are not seriously unwell, also with a contamination rate of 25 per cent
